title: Cron-like schedules: wrap-around weekday ranges, L/#/L-n items, explicit DOM/DOW OR rule, next/previous with 8-year horizon

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 1: exactly five fields, otherwise CronSyntaxError with field=None.
Rule 2: macros matched case-insensitively with their expansions; unknown @text -> field None, item = stripped expression; rule 11 next/previous.
Rule 3: field ranges (minute 0-59, hour 0-23, dom 1-31, month 1-12, dow 0-7); rule 12 field/item.
Rule 3: month names only in month, day names only in day_of_week, case-insensitive.
Rule 4: V > W is an error except in day_of_week (wraps).
Rule 4: S must be a decimal integer >= 1; a step larger than the sequence yields its first element; V/S means V-max/S; lists combine items.
Rule 4: an empty item is an error; rule 12 item ''.
Rule 5: L / L-n (1 <= n <= 30) only in day_of_month, never with a step, allowed in lists.
Rule 6: V#K with 1 <= K <= 5 and VL only in day_of_week, never with a step or range, allowed in lists.
Rule 7: ? only as the entire day_of_month or day_of_week field.
Rule 1: leading/trailing spaces and tabs stripped; fields separated by one or more spaces/tabs.
Rule 3: both 0 and 7 mean Sunday.
Rule 4: day_of_week V > W wraps V..6,0..W; a range start of 7 is 0, an end of 7 stays 7 (5-7 = Fri, Sat, Sun).
Rule 4: * in day_of_week means 0-6 for steps; V/S = V-6/S; steps apply to the (wrapped) sequence (MON-SUN/2 = Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun).
Rule 4: */S takes every S-th value starting at the first (months 1, 4, 7, 10).
Rule 9: both day fields restricted -> a day matches when either matches.
Rule 8: only exactly * or ? is unrestricted; */2, 0-7 and 1-31 are restricted (so OR applies).
Rules 7-9: ? means *; with one restricted field only that field decides.
Rule 9: OR semantics with an impossible day_of_month still matches the weekday; month must match.
Rules 5 and 9: L OR MON.
Rule 9: the month field must always match.
Rule 11: earliest matching datetime with second=0/microsecond=0 strictly later than when.
Rule 11: latest match strictly earlier than when (from 10:00:30 it can return 10:00:00).
Rule 10: matches ignores seconds and microseconds.
Rules 3/11: day 31 only matches months that have it (forward and backward).
Rule 5: L is the last day of the month (leap years); rule 11 previous_before.
Rule 5: L-n is n days before the last day; before the 1st it matches nothing that month.
Rule 6: V#K is the K-th such weekday; #5 only in months that have one; 7 is Sunday.
Rule 6: VL is the last such weekday of the month (5L, friL, 7L).
Rule 11: search window through year when.year + 8 (backward when.year - 8); 2100 is not a leap year.
Rule 11: matches in year when.year + 8 are found, none beyond -> None (same backward with when.year - 8).
Rule 11: no match in the window -> None (next and previous).
Rule 4 range steps (9-17/4 = 9, 13, 17) and rule 11 across a weekend.
Rule 11: occurrences returns up to count consecutive next_after results, stopping at None.
Public API: a datetime with tzinfo raises ValueError for matches, next_after and previous_before.
